title: Canonical atlas direct-image section diagram on the enlarged etale site
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $p:U\to X$ an etale map from a scheme, not necessarily surjective. Regard schemes as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Put $R=U\times_XU$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with projections $p_1,p_2$, $a=f p$ and $b=f p p_1=f p p_2$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $F_U=p^*F$, $F_R=p_1^*F_U\simeq p_2^*F_U$, using the tensor pullbacks and specified chart-limit direct images of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $\widetilde F$ be the extension to $\mathcal C_X$ of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. For every etale scheme $V\to Y$, put $W=V\times_YX$, $Z=V\times_YU$, $Q=V\times_YR$. There are canonical $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear identifications $(f_*F)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(W)$, $(a_*F_U)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(Z)$ and $(b_*F_R)(V)\simeq\widetilde F(Q)$. Under them the canonical map $f_*F\to a_*F_U$ is restriction along $Z\to W$, and the two maps $a_*F_U\rightrightarrows b_*F_R$ are restriction along $Q\rightrightarrows Z$ induced by $p_1,p_2$. The identifications and all three arrows are natural in $V$ and $F$ and preserve every specified scheme-chart projection of the direct-image limits. The scalar actions on all three section modules come from pullback of regular functions along the maps to $V$.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), extension to X_spaces,etale and identification of the three section terms and restriction arrows.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $R$ is a scheme. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], $p_1,p_2$ and $R\to X$ are etale, and $W,Z,Q\to X$ are etale: they are respectively base changes of $V\to Y$ and composites with $p$ or $R\to X$. Thus all three are objects of $\mathcal C_X$. The enlarged model [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] identifies $\mathcal C_U$ with $\mathcal C_X/U$ and $\mathcal C_R$ with $\mathcal C_X/R$, with the restricted structure rings. No use of surjectivity of $p$ is made.

Apply [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] to the etale maps $p,p_1,p_2$ and $R\to X$. It identifies their specified tensor pullbacks with restriction and identifies their specified units with the tensor units. The section formula is $c\otimes m\mapsto cm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Hence the extension of $F_U$ has value $\widetilde F(T)$ at $T\to U$, and the extension of $F_R$ has value $\widetilde F(T)$ at $T\to R$. Both paths through $p_1$ and $p_2$ use this same value: the cited composition formula sends $c\otimes(d\otimes m)$ to $c\,p_i^\sharp(d)\otimes m$, which becomes multiplication followed by restriction. This fixes the canonical identification of the two descriptions of $F_R$.

Apply [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections] to $(f,F)$, $(a,F_U)$ and $(b,F_R)$. The latter two vertices, using step 2, are $\widetilde F(Z)$ and $\widetilde F(Q)$; the first is $\widetilde F(W)$. For each map $l=f,a,b$ the comparison is characterized by $\pi_{T,d}(s)=s|_T$ for every chart $(T,d)\in\mathcal A(l,V)$. This proves the three claimed identifications for the specified direct images of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], retaining all their projections, including when the all-chart category is larger than the module universe.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), first paragraph of proof; chart-limit normalization of the direct-image evaluation.

proof.text: Compute the canonical first arrow as $f_*\eta^p_F$ followed by the projection-preserving direct-image composition comparison of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization]. On the enlarged localized sites of step 1 the tensor unit sends $s$ to $1\otimes s|_{W\times_XU}$, which step 2 sends to $s|_{W\times_XU}$. This is precisely the unit normalization in [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], checked on each scheme chart and hence on enlarged sections by the limiting-cone statement of [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections]. The fibre-product isomorphism $W\times_XU\simeq Z$ sends $((v,x),u)$ to $(v,u)$ and its inverse sends $(v,u)$ to $((v,p(u)),u)$; these formulas mean the universal projection maps. Therefore the arrow is $s\mapsto s|_Z$, and its projection to any chart $T\to Z$ is $s|_T$.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), restriction arrow; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), unit.

proof.text: Apply the same unit computation to each $p_i:R\to U$ and $F_U$, and then apply $a_*$, using the same projection-preserving composition comparison [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization]. The fibre-product comparison $(V\times_YU)\times_UR\simeq V\times_YR$ is $((v,u),r)\mapsto(v,r)$ with inverse $(v,r)\mapsto((v,p_i(r)),r)$. Thus the $i$th arrow sends $t\in\widetilde F(Z)$ to its restriction along $q_i:Q\to Z$, $(v,r)\mapsto(v,p_i(r))$. The two descriptions of the target coincide by step 2; they introduce no extra automorphism of $F_R$. On a chart $T\to Q$ its value is $t|_{q_iT}$, by the projection formula of [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections].

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), the two restriction maps t and s in the proof.

proof.text: The comparisons of step 3 are natural in $V$ and module maps by [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections]. For $V'\to V$, the induced maps of $W,Z,Q$ commute with $Z\to W$ and both $q_i$, since their projections are $(v',x)\mapsto(v,x)$ and the analogous maps with $u,r$. Contravariant functoriality of restrictions therefore makes all three arrow squares commute. A module morphism commutes with these restrictions by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $c\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$, every chart component is multiplication by its pullback along $T\to V$, as specified in the limiting cone. The maps to $V$ agree on both sides of each restriction arrow, so each arrow is $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear. These same component formulas verify preservation of every specified chart projection.
